subject: Nightingale Systems — Private VPC sustained p95 lag & exec escalation
messages:
From: Alicia Barnes <alicia.barnes@nightingale-systems.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: support@nightingale-systems.com
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 latency spike in our private VPC (production)

Hi Naomi,

We started seeing sustained p95 latency rise across our Nightingale private deployment this morning (since ~08:30 PT). Token-level latency has climbed from ~220ms to 1.4s on median workloads; top-percentiles are worse and customers are complaining. We're also seeing a small uptick in 5xx errors tied to decoder timeouts.

Impact: multiple patient-facing endpoints are timing out and our SLO dashboard is red. This is production, high severity.

What we've tried: restarted a handful of workers (no change), scaled the node pool up 2x (temporary relief then back to degraded), and cleared KV cache on one shard (no measurable effect cluster-wide).

Attaching logs and a small sample of queries. Can we get immediate help — this looks like something in the private runtime or a kernel mismatch with our quantized model. We may need an exec-level escalation if this doesn't stabilize in the next 2 hours.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Barnes
Head of ML Ops, Nightingale Systems
attachments: nightingale_log_bundle_20280315.tar.gz, query-sample-20280315.csv

Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 latency spike in our private VPC (production)

Hi Alicia — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're triaging immediately.

Quick notes:
- I've kicked off an end-to-end tracing capture across both regions you use; that will show where time is spent (runtime vs kernel vs network).
- Asked SRE (Jonas) to validate kernel selection and quantization flags; sometimes a fallback to a non-optimized kernel will cause the exact pattern you describe.
- If you can, keep the node scale for now (we'll coordinate rollback of any changes later).

I'll update within 30 minutes with initial findings. If we confirm a regression that impacts SLA, I'll loop in leadership for an exec sync and approval for priority remediation (hotpatch or coordinated rollback).

Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 latency spike in our private VPC (production)

Naomi / Karthik — quick ops update after initial trace:
- Traces show a sharp increase in decoder kernel time at the 2nd-stage attention op on a subset of shards. CPU usage on those workers is fine; GPU kernels are queuing.
- Kernel selector for the quantized 8-bit variant appears to have fallen back to a generic matmul path on 3 nodes (likely due to a micro-upgrade in the private runtime we pushed last night).
- KV cache hit rates are normal; this is not a cache-pressure issue.

Immediate action: rolling a targeted hotfix that forces the optimized kernel selection on affected nodes and draining+repopulating their routing tables. Estimate 45-60 minutes to push and validate. If we can't stabilize, we should consider a rollback of last night's runtime change (needs exec OK).

I'll proceed with the hotfix in 5 minutes unless objections.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia.barnes@nightingale-systems.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 latency spike in our private VPC (production)

Alicia — we identified the likely cause: a private runtime micro-release (rolled in the control plane late last night) caused kernel selection to fallback on a small subset of nodes running your quantized model. Jonas is pushing a targeted hotfix now that forces the optimized kernel path and will drain/repopulate routing for the impacted shards.

Planned timeline: hotfix push (10:20 PT) -> validate p95 and error-rate (10:40 PT) -> follow-up report. We'll open a PD incident and will share the incident link so your on-call can track.

Immediate ask from your side: if you have any custom model variants pinned in the deployment config (model_variant or model_flags), please share those values so we can cross-check kernel mapping.

We will escalate to execs if the hotfix does not restore baseline within 60 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — prioritizing this.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
attachments: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1NightLogs
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Nightingale post-mortem summary & exec ask

TL;DR: Hotfix to force optimized kernel selection on affected nodes restored p95 from ~1.4s back to ~240ms and 5xx errors returned to baseline within ~35 minutes. Root cause: an unintended control-plane flag flip in the 20280311 micro-release caused kernel selector heuristics to prefer a safe generic path for certain quantized shapes.

What we did:
- Applied targeted hotfix (forced kernel selector) + drained/repopulated routing for 6 affected shards (10:20–10:55 PT).
- Validated with synthetic traffic and customer traces; p95 and error rates stable.
- Reverted the micro-release flag in the control plane to restore normal automatic kernel selection.

Impact and current status:
- Customer impact window: ~08:30–11:00 PT on 2028-03-12. No data loss, CPU/GPU health unaffected. Customer-facing endpoints experienced degraded UX and exceeded internal SLAs during that window.

Requested exec approvals:
- Formal SLA credit: customer requests consideration for a partial credit (they estimate business impact). Approve discretionary credit up to two weeks of committed capacity?
- Priority change-control: require an exception for any future kernel-selection heuristic changes for Private customers until we ship an automated canary for quantized variants.

Attachments for review: nightingale_log_bundle_20280315.tar.gz, query-sample-20280315.csv

Next steps:
1) Formal post-mortem doc (ops) — Jonas to own and deliver by EOD tomorrow.
2) Action: add automated canary & gating for kernel-selection heuristic changes (Karthik to scope).
3) Commercial: Naomi to coordinate SLA credit conversation with Nightingale; request customer impact assessment and financial ask.

I'll route this to leadership and finance for credit approval if we get a yes from ops on the PM.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
